standard.name: \(C^2\) differentiability sufficient to state one-dimensional Morse nondegeneracy

assumptions.condition: The critical order satisfies \(1\le m\le k-1\).

novel.justification: The index records the largest permitted vanishing order of the intervention-contrast derivative. Finite Fourier and periodic spline contrasts with controlled multiplicities furnish every value \(1\le m\le k-1\); the index is imposed for quantitative recovery and is not inferred from a Morse perturbation theorem.

assumptions.condition: Relative to \(\lambda^n\), the observational latent density factorizes as \(p_\theta^{\mathrm{obs}}(x)=\prod_{i\in[n]}p_i(x_i\mid x_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)})\) for a DAG \(G\).

For every \(i\in[n]\) and \(e\in\{0,1\}\), the density relative to \(\lambda^n\) is \(p_\theta^{i,e}(x)=q_i^e(x_i)\prod_{j\ne i}p_j(x_j\mid x_{\operatorname{pa}_G(j)})\), where \(q_i^e\) is normalized relative to \(d\lambda(t)=dt/(2\pi)\).
The learner observes the observational environment and both environments \((i,0),(i,1)\) in every target group, while the node names are known only up to one common permutation in \(\mathfrak S_n\).

standard.name: Coupled hard-intervention groups with unknown node permutation

assumptions.condition: Every complete latent density satisfies \(c_0\le p_\theta^a(x)\le C_0\) for all \(a\in\mathcal A\) and \(x\in\mathbb T^n\).

standard.name: Two-sided bounded-density overlap on compact support

assumptions.condition: Every complete latent density satisfies \(\lVert p_\theta^a\rVert_{C^k(\mathbb T^n)}\le K\).

novel.justification: A common \(C^k\) envelope rules out increasingly oscillatory complete laws that keep Hellinger error small while moving the inverse map at finer scales. Bounded trigonometric causal mechanisms on the compact torus satisfy the envelope for a fixed \(K\).

assumptions.condition: The decoder and encoder satisfy \(\lVert f\rVert_{C^k}+\lVert f^{-1}\rVert_{C^k}\le K\).

novel.justification: A uniform \(C^k\) envelope prevents decoder perturbations from concentrating below the scale resolved by the law discrepancy. Periodic shears \(f_\delta(x)=(x_1+\delta\sin x_2,x_2,\ldots,x_n)\) with \(|\delta|<1/2\) form a nontrivial bounded family.

assumptions.condition: Every singular value of \(Df(x)\) lies in \([K^{-1},K]\) for every \(x\in\mathbb T^n\).

novel.justification: Uniform singular-value bounds keep observed-law and latent-law norms mutually comparable and exclude Jacobian collapse as an alternative source of instability. The periodic shear family has determinant one and uniformly bounded map and inverse derivatives.

assumptions.condition: Each marked set satisfies \(|Z_{\theta i}|\le J\).

novel.justification: Periodic intervention profiles used for circular controls have finitely many turning points; a fixed trigonometric degree or spline knot budget gives a uniform value of \(J\).

assumptions.condition: For every \(i\in[n]\), distinct points \(z,z'\in Z_{\theta i}\) satisfy \(\operatorname{dist}_{\mathbb T}(z,z')\ge\Delta_0\).

novel.justification: A fixed separation prevents critical neighborhoods from coalescing as the law varies, which would create an additional unresolved scale in a uniform modulus. Fixed-degree Fourier contrasts and periodic splines with separated knots satisfy the condition.

assumptions.condition: For every \(i\in[n]\) and \(t\in\mathbb T\), \(|r_{\theta i}'(t)|\ge a_0\operatorname{dist}_{\mathbb T}(t,Z_{\theta i})^m\), with the same constant \(a_0\) for every node and model.

novel.justification: This is a uniform finite-type rate condition, not a consequence of quantitative Morse theory. The periodic family \(r_i(t)=b_i\gamma_m(t)-\log Z_i\), with \(\gamma_1(t)=1-\cos t\) and \(\gamma_m(t)=\sin(t)^{m+1}/(m+1)\) for \(m\ge2\), has separated zeros of order at most \(m\), including zeros of exact order \(m\), and satisfies the displayed margin for constants fixed by \(b_i\).

assumptions.condition: For every \(a\in\mathcal A\), the data contain \(N\) independent draws from \(P_\theta^a\), and samples are independent across environments.
For every \(i\in[n]\), there is \(z_i\in Z_{\theta i}\) such that, for every lift increment \(|u|\le\min\{\Delta_0/4,1\}\), \(a_0|u|^m\le |r_{\theta i}'(z_i+u)|\le K|u|^m\).

novel.justification: The condition makes the class index \(m\) an attained worst critical order rather than a loose upper label. The displayed trigonometric family attains order \(m\) at \(0\) and \(\pi\), while its remaining critical points have no larger order.

assumptions.condition: For every \(i\in\{1,2\}\) and \(z\in Z_{\theta i}\), the one-dimensional Hessian satisfies \(|r_{\theta i}''(z)|\ge a_0\).

standard.name: Nondegenerate critical point for a \(C^2\) function

definitions.name: Symmetric quotient encoder pseudometric
definitions.construction: For one alignment \((\pi,\phi)\in\mathfrak S_n\ltimes\mathrm{Diff}(\mathbb T)^n\), set \(L_{\theta\leftarrow\widetilde\theta}(\pi,\phi)^2=\int\sum_{i\in[n]}\operatorname{dist}_{\mathbb T}\{h_{\theta i}(y),\phi_i(h_{\widetilde\theta,\pi(i)}(y))\}^2d\bar P_\theta(y)\) and \(L_{\widetilde\theta\leftarrow\theta}(\pi,\phi)^2=\int\sum_{j\in[n]}\operatorname{dist}_{\mathbb T}\{h_{\widetilde\theta j}(y),\phi_{\pi^{-1}(j)}^{-1}(h_{\theta,\pi^{-1}(j)}(y))\}^2d\bar P_{\widetilde\theta}(y)\). Define \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta,\widetilde\theta)=\inf_{\pi,\phi}\max\{L_{\theta\leftarrow\widetilde\theta}(\pi,\phi),L_{\widetilde\theta\leftarrow\theta}(\pi,\phi)\}\). The same alignment and its algebraic inverse are used in the two directions.

definitions.name: Coordinate baseline gauge
definitions.construction: Because \(q_i^0\) is a density with respect to \(d\lambda(s)=ds/(2\pi)\), define the lift \(\overline\beta_{\theta i}(t)=\int_0^tq_i^0(s)ds\). Then \(\overline\beta_{\theta i}(t+2\pi)=\overline\beta_{\theta i}(t)+2\pi\) and \(\overline\beta_{\theta i}'=q_i^0>0\), so \(\beta_{\theta i}=\overline\beta_{\theta i}\pmod{2\pi}\) is an orientation-preserving degree-one circle diffeomorphism and \((\beta_{\theta i})_*(q_i^0d\lambda)=d\lambda\). Set \(\beta_\theta=(\beta_{\theta1},\ldots,\beta_{\theta n})\) and \(F_\theta=f\circ\beta_\theta^{-1}\).

definitions.name: Determinant--factorization residual
definitions.construction: For the group permutation minimizing \(D_H\), let \(T=T_{\theta,\widetilde\theta}\), \(R_i=r_{\theta i}\circ\beta_{\theta i}^{-1}\), and \(S_i=r_{\widetilde\theta,\pi(i)}\circ\beta_{\widetilde\theta,\pi(i)}^{-1}\). Then \(\mathcal E(\theta,\widetilde\theta)=\lVert|\det DT|-1\rVert_{L^2(\lambda^n)}+\{\sum_{i\in[n]}\lVert R_i\circ T_i-S_i\rVert_{L^2(\lambda^n)}^2\}^{1/2}\).

definitions.name: Two-plane cylindrical Hamiltonian lower family
definitions.construction: Fix the empty graph \(G_0\), the identity decoder \(f_0\), uniform observational and baseline densities \(p_0^{\mathrm{obs}}=q_i^0=1\) with respect to \(\lambda^n\) and \(\lambda\), and \(q_i^1(t)=Z_i^{-1}\exp\{b_i\gamma_m(t)\}\), where \(Z_i=\int_{\mathbb T}\exp\{b_i\gamma_m(t)\}d\lambda(t)\) and \(0<b_1<\cdots<b_n<1\). Then the log-ratio derivatives have exact order \(m\) at zero. In the injective chart \((-R_0,R_0)^2\times\mathbb T^{n-2}\), write \(x_{12}=(x_1,x_2)\), \(r=|x_{12}|\), and \(\alpha_h(r)=\tau h^{k-1}\eta(r^2/h^2)\) for \(0<h<R_0/2\). Define \(\Psi_h(x)=(\operatorname{Rot}(\alpha_h(r))x_{12},x_3,\ldots,x_n)\) on the cylinder \(\{r<h\}\times\mathbb T^{n-2}\) and \(\Psi_h(x)=x\) outside it. The cutoff makes the chart extension smooth, \(\Psi_h^{-1}\) is obtained by replacing \(\alpha_h\) by \(-\alpha_h\), and \(\det D\Psi_h=1+(\nabla\alpha_h)^\top J_2x_{12}=1\). For \(0\le j\le k\), \(\lVert D^j(\Psi_h-\mathrm{id})\rVert_\infty+\lVert D^j(\Psi_h^{-1}-\mathrm{id})\rVert_\infty\le C\tau h^{k-j}\). Let \(\theta_0=(G_0,p_0,q_0,f_0)\) and \(\theta_h=(G_0,p_0,q_0,f_0\circ\Psi_h^{-1})\).

definitions.name: Restricted two-plane radial inverse modulus
definitions.construction: Fix \(n\), the empty graph, the same positive product mechanisms used in Definition \(\mathrm{def:hamiltonian\text{-}lower\text{-}family}\), and fixed constants \((c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\) containing that family. For \(a\in C_c^\infty([0,R_0^2))\), write \(x_{12}=(x_1,x_2)\), \(r=|x_{12}|\), let \(\Psi_a(x)=(\operatorname{Rot}(a(r^2))x_{12},x_3,\ldots,x_n)\) in the \(E_{12}\) chart cylinder, and extend it by the identity outside \(\{r<R_0\}\times\mathbb T^{n-2}\); this map satisfies \(\det D\Psi_a=1\). Let \(\theta_a=(G_0,p_0,q_0,\Psi_a^{-1})\). Then \(\Omega_{k,m}^{\mathrm{rad}}(\varepsilon)=\sup\{d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta_a,\theta_{\widetilde a}):\ \theta_a,\theta_{\widetilde a}\in\mathcal M_{n,k,m}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0),\ \lVert a\rVert_\infty\vee\lVert\widetilde a\rVert_\infty\le\alpha_0,\ \lVert\Psi_a\rVert_{C^k}+\lVert\Psi_a^{-1}\rVert_{C^k}\le K,\ \lVert\Psi_{\widetilde a}\rVert_{C^k}+\lVert\Psi_{\widetilde a}^{-1}\rVert_{C^k}\le K,\ D_H(\theta_a,\theta_{\widetilde a})\le\varepsilon\}\). Thus the plane, cylindrical support, fixed mechanisms, model bounds, volume preservation, map and inverse bounds, complete-family law metric, and full permutation--coordinate quotient loss are all part of the restricted supremum.

definitions.name: Auditable two-node \(C^2\) Morse instance
definitions.construction: Set \(n=2\), \(k=2\), \(m=1\), \(G_0\) empty, \(f_0=\mathrm{id}\), \(p_0^{\mathrm{obs}}=q_1^0=q_2^0=1\), and \(q_i^1(t)=Z_i^{-1}\exp\{b_i(1-\cos t)\}\), where \(0<b_1<b_2<1\) and \(Z_i=\int_{\mathbb T}\exp\{b_i(1-\cos t)\}d\lambda(t)\). Thus \(r_i'(t)=b_i\sin t\), \(Z_i=\{0,\pi\}\), and \(|r_i''(z)|=b_i\) at both critical points. Let \(\theta_0=(G_0,p_0,q_0,\mathrm{id})\). For \(0<h<R_0/2\), set \(\alpha_h(r)=\tau h\eta(r^2/h^2)\), \(\Psi_h(x)=\operatorname{Rot}(\alpha_h(|x|))x\) on \(|x|<h\), and the identity outside the chart; define \(\theta_h=(G_0,p_0,q_0,\Psi_h^{-1})\).

definitions.name: Morse incompressible-rigidity handle
definitions.construction: First use the synthetic product law and a Dacorogna--Moser correction to separate determinant distortion from a normalized volume-preserving map; then apply a Hodge decomposition, prove weighted \(C^k\) interpolation for its zero-fiber-mean divergence-free component, and absorb the determinant and ratio nonlinear remainders without losing the top derivative.

definitions.name: Positive Fourier minimum-distance estimator
definitions.construction: For every \(a\in\mathcal A\), the observed density relative to \(\lambda^n\) is at least \(c_0/K^n\), because \(dP_\theta^a/d\lambda^n(y)=p_\theta^a(f^{-1}(y))/|\det Df(f^{-1}(y))|\) and every singular value of \(Df\) is at most \(K\). Put \(\ell_0=c_0/(2K^n)\), \(g_L^a(y)=\max\{N^{-1},\operatorname{Re}\sum_{\|\ell\|_\infty\le L_N}\widehat c_{a\ell}e^{\mathrm i\ell^\top y}\}\), and \(\widehat p_L^a(y)=\ell_0+(1-\ell_0)g_L^a(y)/\int g_L^a d\lambda^n\). This density integrates to one and remains at least \(c_0/(2K^n)\) after normalization. Enumerate a rational wrapped-spline sieve of mechanisms and lifts \(Az+u(z)\), with \(A\) in the bounded subset of \(GL(n,\mathbb Z)\), and retain only candidates certified by interval arithmetic to satisfy the class bounds, positive Jacobian, degree one, and the finite-type profile. Define \(\widehat\theta_N\) as a certified approximate minimizer of the complete-family Hellinger criterion against \((\widehat p_L^a:a\in\mathcal A)\).

definitions.name: Inverted complete-law confidence set
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C_N(\alpha)=\{[h_\vartheta]:\vartheta\in\mathcal M_{n,k,m}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0),\ D_H(\vartheta,\widehat\theta_N)\le c_\alpha\rho_N+\delta_N\}\), where \(c_\alpha\) is calibrated from simultaneous spectral concentration and \(\delta_N\) is the certified sieve and optimization tolerance.

definitions.name: Critical-order adaptation handle
definitions.construction: Use dyadic spectral estimates of each \(r_{\theta i}'\) to test nested finite-type orders, exclude profiles within the minimax testing radius of a lower-order class, select the smallest accepted order, and invert the corresponding complete-law ball using the order-specific modulus.

definitions.name: Primary two-node \(C^2\) Morse class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{Morse}}_{2,2,1}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)=\{\theta\in\mathcal M_{2,2,1}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0):\theta\text{ satisfies Assumption }\mathrm{ass:primary\text{-}morse\text{-}hessian}\}\). The indices are fixed at \(n=2\), \(k=2\), and \(m=1\); membership is justified by the displayed \(C^2\) derivative and Hessian conditions and not by a quantitative-Morse perturbation theorem.

definitions.name: Bounded torus mechanism and decoder example
definitions.construction: Fix an empty DAG, product observational density one, \(q_i^0=1\), and \(q_i^1(t)=Z_i^{-1}\exp\{b_i\gamma_m(t)\}\) with distinct \(0<b_i<1\). For \(|\delta|<1/2\), let \(f_\delta(x)=(x_1+\delta\sin x_2,x_2,\ldots,x_n)\pmod{2\pi}\), whose inverse is \(f_\delta^{-1}(y)=(y_1-\delta\sin y_2,y_2,\ldots,y_n)\) and whose Jacobian determinant is one. Set \(\theta_\delta=(G_\varnothing,p_\delta,q_\delta,f_\delta)\).

statements.statement: The functional \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}\) is nonnegative and symmetric, is unchanged when either encoder is relabeled by a node permutation and coordinatewise circle diffeomorphisms, vanishes on every such common quotient class, and obeys the quotient triangle inequality. Moreover, on the bounded-density and bi-Lipschitz class it is uniformly equivalent to either directed aligned \(L^2\) loss, so replacing the reference model by its competitor cannot change a modulus exponent.
statements.justification: A law-to-representation modulus and a confidence-set diameter require an order-free quotient geometry rather than a loss directed from one selected model.
statements.gap: The exact-identification papers specify an equivalence class but do not metrize approximate encoder recovery under two competing observed laws.
statements.consumer: Every lower bound, upper modulus, estimator guarantee, and confidence-set diameter uses the same symmetric quotient object.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(n\ge2\), \(k\ge2\), and \(1\le m\le k-1\), there are constants \((c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\) and a nonzero interval of \(\delta\) for which every model \(\theta_\delta\) in Definition \(\mathrm{def:bounded\text{-}rate\text{-}class\text{-}example}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_{n,k,m}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\). The decoder is nonlinear, degree one, volume preserving, uniformly bi-Lipschitz, and bounded with its inverse in \(C^k\); the mechanisms are positive bounded periodic densities and attain critical order \(m\).
statements.justification: The strengthened uniform rate envelopes define a concrete nonempty causal class rather than an oracle regularity shell.
statements.gap: Exact-identification results allow broader qualitative classes, while a uniform inverse modulus needs explicit control of oscillation and Jacobian conditioning.
statements.consumer: The example calibrates admissible constants for simulations and supplies a baseline family for sharpness constructions.

statements.statement: On the shared circular perfect-intervention setting, Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass:perfect\text{-}intervention\text{-}family}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:complete\text{-}grouping}\) retain the node-target intervention structure used by Liang et al. and Varıcı et al. Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass:density\text{-}smoothness}\), \(\mathrm{ass:decoder\text{-}smoothness}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:decoder\text{-}conditioning}\) strictly strengthen their qualitative envelopes for uniform rates. Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass:critical\text{-}cardinality}\), \(\mathrm{ass:critical\text{-}separation}\), \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}type\text{-}profile}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}type\text{-}attainment}\) replace an almost-everywhere nonzero discrepancy by a quantitative isolated-zero condition, which implies nonzero discrepancy almost everywhere. Consequently, at \(D_H=0\) the proposed quotient conclusion agrees with their componentwise exact-identification conclusion on the shared subclass; the new claim concerns only the nonzero-error rate.
statements.justification: A theorem-level hypothesis map distinguishes inherited exact identification from the strengthened assumptions that buy a uniform modulus.
statements.gap: The comparator papers establish exact recovery but do not separate which of their assumptions control identification and which additional envelopes would control a law-based rate.
statements.consumer: Referees and users can identify precisely when the modulus specializes to the published exact results and what extra regularity is paid for quantitative stability.

statements.statement: For every \(\theta\in\mathcal M_{n,k,m}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\), \(B_\theta\) is a density with respect to \(\lambda^n\), \(\int B_\theta d\lambda^n=1\), and \(B_\theta d\lambda^n=f_*[\{\prod_{i\in[n]}q_i^0\}d\lambda^n]\). The identity holds for every DAG \(G\).
statements.justification: This observable invariant removes both models' DAG and mechanism nuisance before any rigidity argument.
statements.gap: Dacorogna--Moser characterize the Jacobian channel and Liang et al. use individual likelihood ratios; neither inspected source states this complete causal product cancellation.
statements.consumer: The invariant supplies determinant control needed to reject ratio-only strip alternatives in every complete-family fit.

statements.statement: There is a class-uniform constant \(C\) such that, after an optimizing group permutation and the coordinate baseline gauges, \(\mathcal E(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\le C D_H(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\) for all \(\theta,\widetilde\theta\in\mathcal M_{n,k,m}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\).
statements.justification: It converts the statistical law metric into the exact analytic defects that can control the density quotient and its incompressible kernel.
statements.gap: Khesin et al. identify Hellinger geometry only on the density quotient; the intervention-ratio terms needed to control the quotient fiber are absent there.
statements.consumer: Every population and finite-sample recovery statement can work with observable Hellinger error rather than unobservable score identities.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(n\ge2\), \(k\ge2\), and \(1\le m\le k-1\), there exist fixed constants \((c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\) and distinct smooth positive mechanisms such that the empty-DAG models \(\theta_0,\theta_h\) from Definition \(\mathrm{def:hamiltonian\text{-}lower\text{-}family}\) belong to \(\mathcal M_{n,k,m}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\) for every sufficiently small \(h\). The trigonometric contrasts obey the common finite-type margin, have uniformly separated critical points, and attain order \(m\). The perturbation is supported on \(\{|x_{12}|<h\}\times\mathbb T^{n-2}\), preserves \(\lambda^n\) exactly, and satisfies the displayed uniform \(C^k\) envelope for both \(\Psi_h\) and \(\Psi_h^{-1}\). In the case \((n,k,m)=(2,2,1)\), both models also belong to \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{Morse}}_{2,2,1}\).
statements.justification: Membership must be proved, rather than assumed, so the converse lives in one fixed nondegenerate class.
statements.gap: CauCA's plateau rotation does not belong to the finite-type class and does not supply a small nonzero law discrepancy.
statements.consumer: This proposition makes the lower modulus applicable to the same bounded class used by the upper theorem.

statements.statement: For each fixed \(n\ge2\), the cylindrical two-plane models in Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:lower\text{-}family\text{-}membership}\) satisfy \(D_H(\theta_0,\theta_h)\asymp_n h^{k+m+1}\) and \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta_0,\theta_h)\asymp_n h^{k+1}\). Only environments targeting coordinates one and two change; integration over the inactive \(\mathbb T^{n-2}\) factor equals one under \(\lambda^{n-2}\), so the active support has two-dimensional volume order \(h^2\) and the powers do not contain \(n\). Constants may depend on the fixed dimension through the family size and mixture normalization. Hence every fixed class containing this family satisfies \(\Omega_{k,m}(\varepsilon)\ge c_n\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\) for all sufficiently small \(\varepsilon\). The two directed aligned losses have the same leading order, so the conclusion holds for the symmetric quotient pseudometric.
statements.justification: The lower family certifies the exponent and proves that coordinatewise reparameterizations cannot absorb the leading mixed motion.
statements.gap: Liang et al. construct exact plateau rotations; this theorem instead gives a finite-criticality local alternative with explicit nonzero Hellinger and quotient orders.
statements.consumer: The result supplies the sharpness benchmark for any recovery algorithm or confidence radius on circular latent variables.

statements.statement: In Definition \(\mathrm{def:primary\text{-}morse\text{-}instance}\), \(\theta_0,\theta_h\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm{Morse}}_{2,2,1}\), \(\beta_1=\beta_2=\mathrm{id}\), \(\det D\Psi_h=1\), and \(\lVert\Psi_h-\mathrm{id}\rVert_\infty=O(h^2)\), \(\lVert D(\Psi_h-\mathrm{id})\rVert_\infty=O(h)\), and \(\lVert D^2(\Psi_h-\mathrm{id})\rVert_\infty=O(1)\), with the same bounds for the inverse. The observational and two baseline contributions are exactly zero: \(H^2(P_{\theta_0}^{\mathrm{obs}},P_{\theta_h}^{\mathrm{obs}})=H^2(P_{\theta_0}^{1,0},P_{\theta_h}^{1,0})=H^2(P_{\theta_0}^{2,0},P_{\theta_h}^{2,0})=0\). For \(i=1,2\), \[h^{-8}H^2(P_{\theta_0}^{i,1},P_{\theta_h}^{i,1})\longrightarrow c_i:=\frac{b_i^2q_i^1(0)\tau^2}{8(2\pi)^2}\int_{|\xi|<1}\xi_i^2\eta(|\xi|^2)^2(J_2\xi)_i^2d\xi>0.\] Since \(b_1\ne b_2\), a wrong group permutation has a fixed positive limiting cost, and therefore \(D_H(\theta_0,\theta_h)=C_Hh^4\{1+o(1)\}\), where \(C_H^2=c_1+c_2\). The synthetic products satisfy \(B_{\theta_0}=B_{\theta_h}=1\), so the synthetic-law Hellinger residual and \(\lVert|\det D\Psi_h|-1\rVert_{L^2(\lambda^2)}\) are zero. Writing \(\overline p_0(0)=\{3+q_1^1(0)+q_2^1(0)\}/5\), parity gives zero transverse conditional mean for \(\eta(|\xi|^2)J_2\xi\). Conditional variance, even after enlarging the quotient to all measurable coordinate functions, gives the same positive leading coefficient for both directed losses because \(d\bar P_{\theta_h}/d\bar P_{\theta_0}=1+O(h^2)\) on the packet: \[\liminf_{h\downarrow0}h^{-6}d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta_0,\theta_h)^2\ge\frac{\overline p_0(0)\tau^2}{(2\pi)^2}\sum_{i=1}^2\int_{|\xi|<1}\eta(|\xi|^2)^2(J_2\xi)_i^2d\xi>0.\] Every wrong coordinate permutation has fixed positive loss at \(h=0\), and the identity coordinate gauge gives the matching upper order. Hence the symmetric quotient pseudometric satisfies \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta_0,\theta_h)\asymp h^3\), while the complete-law distance is order \(h^4\), yielding the audited power \(3/4\).
statements.justification: The complete \(n=2\), \(C^2\), Morse calculation makes the \(3/4\) lower order auditable environment by environment and through the nonlinear quotient.
statements.gap: CauCA's determinant-one plateau rotation has zero law error; this instance computes the nonzero Hellinger coefficient at isolated Morse points and the surviving quotient coefficient.
statements.consumer: The calculation is the unit test for any proof, implementation, or claimed improvement of the primary recovery exponent.

statements.statement: For each fixed \(n\ge2\), the actual restricted supremum in Definition \(\mathrm{def:radial\text{-}modulus}\) satisfies \(\Omega_{k,m}^{\mathrm{rad}}(\varepsilon)\asymp_n\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\). The active map is a bounded \(C^k\) radial rotation in the named plane \(E_{12}\), supported on a fixed chart cylinder and equal to the identity on coordinates three through \(n\); therefore the interpolation and Hellinger integrals are two-dimensional, while constants may depend on the fixed \(n\). In particular, the audited \(n=2\), \(k=2\), \(m=1\) restriction has exponent \(3/4\).
statements.justification: This nontrivial infinite-dimensional sector verifies the proposed exponent before the arbitrary-map rigidity step.
statements.gap: No inspected causal representation result computes a sharp modulus even on radial nonlinear torus decoders.
statements.consumer: The radial theorem supplies a controlled benchmark and a falsifiable testbed for proofs and numerical recovery procedures.

statements.statement: Determine whether a class-uniform constant \(C\) exists such that every aligned pair \(\theta,\widetilde\theta\in\mathcal M_{n,k,m}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\) obeys \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\le C\mathcal E(\theta,\widetilde\theta)^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\). The primary kill test is \(n=2\), \(k=2\), \(m=1\): prove the normalized weighted inequality for arbitrary bounded divergence-free periodic \(C^2\) fields, or construct a legal joint-critical or oscillatory sequence with an unbounded normalized ratio and then test whether it integrates to a full-law counterexample.
statements.justification: This is the genuinely open analytic content separating a publishable full-class frontier from a radial analogue.
statements.gap: Friesecke--James--Müller control a matrix-well defect and Dacorogna--Moser control a prescribed determinant; neither controls a divergence-free map from Morse-degenerate scalar transport equations.
statements.consumer: An affirmative answer closes the full nuisance-uniform modulus; a negative answer identifies the minimal spacing, profile, or decoder restriction required for valid causal recovery.

statements.statement: For every fixed nondegenerate bounded class \(\mathcal M_{n,k,m}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\) containing the lower family, there exist \(0<c\le C<\infty\) such that \(c\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\le\Omega_{k,m}(\varepsilon)\le C\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\) for all sufficiently small \(\varepsilon\), with \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}\) the symmetric quotient pseudometric. The primary class \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{Morse}}_{2,2,1}\) is justified directly by its \(C^2\) Hessian condition and has exponent \(3/4\). At \(\varepsilon=0\), the finite-type conditions imply almost-everywhere discrepancy and the conclusion agrees with exact componentwise recovery on the shared circular subclass of Liang et al. and Varıcı et al.; the strengthened smoothness, conditioning, separation, and attained-order assumptions are used only for the uniform nonzero-error frontier.
statements.justification: The theorem names the critical-order recovery frontier in a symmetric quotient geometry and separates the directly stated \(C^2\) Morse headline from the novel general finite-type rate class.
statements.gap: Liang et al. and Varıcı et al. prove qualitative exact recovery under almost-everywhere discrepancy; no cited Morse theorem supplies the \(k=2\) rate assumptions, and no comparator gives a symmetric law-based sharp exponent at isolated critical points.
statements.consumer: Likelihood and score-based causal representation learners obtain a calibrated translation from population objective error to encoder error.

statements.statement: When \(n=2\), \(k=2\), and \(m=1\), Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:matching\text{-}full\text{-}modulus}\) gives \(\Omega_{2,1}(\varepsilon)\asymp\varepsilon^{3/4}\); when \(\varepsilon=0\), it reduces to componentwise circular recovery up to a node permutation, consistent with the exact-identification conclusions of Liang et al. and Varıcı et al. Plateaus are outside Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}type\text{-}profile}\) and retain their known rotation ambiguity.
statements.justification: The reduction records both the flagship \(3/4\) case and the required exact-law sanity check.
statements.gap: The exact papers have no rate, while plateau counterexamples do not decide stability at isolated Morse points.
statements.consumer: Two-angle systems, including wrapped robotic joint coordinates, receive an interpretable recovery exponent and a clear failure boundary.

statements.statement: Under independent sampling and for certified tolerance \(\delta_N=o(\rho_N)\), the positive Fourier minimum-distance estimator satisfies \(D_H(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)=O_{\mathbb P}(\rho_N)\) and \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)=O_{\mathbb P}\{\rho_N^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\}\), uniformly over the model class. In the primary case \(n=2\), \(k=2\), \(m=1\), this is \((N/\log N)^{-3/16}\).
statements.justification: A computable estimator turns the population frontier into a usable finite-sample guarantee in the same symmetric quotient geometry, without numerical differentiation at critical points.
statements.gap: Acartürk et al. give finite-sample recovery for linear mixers, and Lyu--Fu control a derivative diagnostic for nonlinear ICA; neither handles bounded nonlinear causal decoders or quotient loss.
statements.consumer: Implementations on periodic latent coordinates obtain a certified stopping rule and representation error radius from environment samples.

statements.statement: For every fixed known \((k,m)\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), the inverted set \(\mathcal C_N(\alpha)\) is uniformly honest, \(\inf_{\theta\in\mathcal M_{n,k,m}}\Pr_\theta\{[h_\theta]\in\mathcal C_N(\alpha)\}\ge1-\alpha-o(1)\), and its diameter measured by the symmetric quotient pseudometric \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}\) is \(O_{\mathbb P}\{\rho_N^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\}\).
statements.justification: The confidence set expresses uncertainty in the identifiable quotient rather than in an arbitrary latent gauge.
statements.gap: Manifold density bands cover the environment laws, while Bull--Nickl cover ordinary \(L^2\) function classes; neither propagates coverage through a critical nonlinear causal quotient.
statements.consumer: Users can report uncertainty for recovered circular factors and compare representations without fixing an unidentifiable coordinate gauge.

statements.statement: Characterize the smallest separation from lower-order or plateau profiles under which one confidence procedure, constructed by the critical-order adaptation handle, is honest over \(m\in\{1,\ldots,k-1\}\) and has diameter of the order-specific rate \(\rho_N^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\); prove a matching impossibility result below that separation.
statements.justification: Unknown critical order is empirically unavoidable, but honest adaptation across nonregular inverse exponents may require an explicit testing margin.
statements.gap: Bull and Nickl characterize smoothness adaptation for ordinary \(L^2\) density sets, not adaptation across causal inverse orders or proximity to a nonidentified plateau.
statements.consumer: The result would tell practitioners when the critical exponent can be learned from data and when a conservative worst-order confidence radius is unavoidable.

sampling_model.design: One observational environment and two grouped positive stochastic perfect-intervention environments for every latent node; group labels are observed up to one common node permutation.
sampling_model.units: \(N\) independent observations from each environment on \(\mathbb T^n\), independent across environments.
sampling_model.treatment: The environment replaces exactly one latent conditional mechanism by a parent-free circular density \(q_i^e\) normalized with respect to \(d\lambda(t)=dt/(2\pi)\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every complete latent law is bounded between \(c_0\) and \(C_0\), and the decoder is uniformly bi-Lipschitz.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Positive truncated Fourier density estimation normalized by a convex floor construction that remains at least \(c_0/(2K^n)\), followed by a certified rational wrapped-spline minimum-distance fit; no derivative of an estimated density is required for the population residual reduction.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Then CauCA in \((G,\mathcal F,\mathcal P_G)\) is identifiable up to \(\mathcal S_{\mathrm{scaling}}\).
Two hard interventions with interventional discrepancy on the same target node suffice to recover that node up to a diffeomorphism.
Then there is \(A\in SO(d)\) such that \(g^{-1}\circ f(s)=As+h(s)+b\).
Algorithms 2 and 3 are consistent estimators of the latent graph and inverse transformation up to the corresponding equivalence classes.
With a large enough \(N\), the estimated cross-derivative vectors are almost zero for all coordinate pairs.

tldr: Complete paired interventions reveal a synthetic product law that controls decoder volume distortion for every DAG. Encoder error is measured by a symmetric quotient pseudometric: one common permutation and coordinatewise circle alignment is evaluated in both directed \(L^2\) losses and their maximum is minimized. The primary \(n=2\), \(C^2\) nondegenerate Morse class is defined directly by separated critical points and a nonzero one-dimensional Hessian, without importing a higher-smoothness quantitative-Morse theorem. A distinct novel finite-type rate class covers \(1\le m\le k-1\) with uniform margins, separation, and attained order, and an explicit periodic mechanism family and nonlinear torus shear certify nonemptiness of the strengthened density, \(C^k\), and bi-Lipschitz envelopes. The explicit Hamiltonian cylinder gives the \(3/4\) Morse lower order and the matching radial frontier. The open contribution remains arbitrary-map incompressible rigidity; an affirmative result yields the full \(\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\) modulus, the Fourier estimator clipped at \(c_0/(2K^n)\), and symmetric-quotient confidence sets.

project_justification.gap: CauCA and score-based causal representation learning establish componentwise exact identification under almost-everywhere intervention discrepancy, but they do not metrize approximate recovery symmetrically or quantify isolated critical zeros. Quantitative Morse perturbation results requiring higher smoothness do not justify the primary \(C^2\) case, and near-isometry robustness controls a different primitive defect.
project_justification.niche: Circular latent coordinates permit a directly stated \(C^2\) Morse class and a separate finite-type hierarchy with exact uniform margins and attained worst order. Complete intervention laws add a determinant channel, while symmetric two-law quotient loss removes dependence on which competing model is declared the reference.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the synthetic product reduction, validates a genuine symmetric quotient geometry, audits the two-node Hamiltonian Morse construction environment by environment, establishes the precise radial restricted frontier, maps its strengthened rate assumptions to the retained exact-identification hypotheses, and targets the nonradial rigidity step needed for estimation and confidence sets.

related_work: Liang et al. establish exact CauCA recovery under almost-everywhere intervention discrepancy and exhibit determinant-one rotations on common plateaus; their exact-identification structure informs the retained intervention assumptions, while Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:identification\text{-}hypothesis\text{-}comparison}\) isolates the stronger envelopes used only for rates. Varıcı et al. derive componentwise and graph recovery from exact sparse score changes under paired node interventions; the proposed symmetric quotient modulus agrees with that qualitative conclusion at zero law error but does not claim to sharpen their theorem. Buchholz and Schölkopf use Friesecke--James--Müller rigidity to quantify near-isometric representation learning; their defect is distance from rotations rather than complete-family Hellinger error. Khesin et al. identify density space as a quotient by volume-preserving diffeomorphisms, motivating the incompressible kernel. Dacorogna--Moser and Teixeira provide prescribed-Jacobian and support-localized volume corrections. Milnor's standard definition of a nondegenerate critical point supports the directly stated \(C^2\) Morse condition. Tạ Lê Lợi and Phan Phiến provide quantitative critical-neighborhood tools under their own higher-smoothness hypotheses; those tools may inform the general finite-type analysis but are not used to justify the primary \(k=2\) class. Acartürk et al. and Lyu--Fu provide finite-sample templates for linear interventional causal representation learning and contrastive nonlinear independent component analysis. Kerkyacharian--Nickl--Picard and Bull--Nickl supply compact-manifold density concentration and confidence-set honesty machinery.
technical_internal_limitation: The decisive full-class upper bound is not established by the radial calculation. Symmetrizing the quotient loss removes reference-law directionality but does not prove the weighted incompressible coercivity inequality. A ratio-only strip perturbation creates a larger determinant error and therefore challenges proofs that discard the synthetic law, not the complete-law frontier. Any analytic counterexample must also integrate to two legal complete causal law families and respect the strengthened rate envelopes.
honest_scope: The primary class has \(n=2\), \(k=2\), \(m=1\), separated critical points, and the direct Hessian bound \(|r_i''(z)|\ge a_0\); it does not rely on a quantitative-Morse theorem that assumes higher differentiability. The general class treats \(1\le m\le k-1\) as a novel finite-type rate condition with common margin \(a_0\), at most \(J\) critical points separated by \(\Delta_0\), and an attained order-\(m\) point for every contrast. Uniform density \(C^k\), decoder \(C^k\), and bi-Lipschitz bounds are strengthened rate-class assumptions, and the explicit periodic mechanisms with nonlinear torus shears show the class is nonempty. Exact plateau rotations and almost-everywhere exact recovery remain prior art. The two-plane lower family has dimension-independent powers only because its active support is two-dimensional and \(\lambda^{n-2}(\mathbb T^{n-2})=1\); constants may depend on fixed \(n\). The radial restricted supremum and the complete two-node calculation are theorem targets. The arbitrary nonradial upper inequality is the first-class open question. Coalescing critical points, critical submanifolds, vector-valued contrast curves, and honest adaptation to unknown \(m\) remain outside the primary claim.

seed_details.question: Does complete-family Hellinger error \(\varepsilon\) force quotient encoder error of exact order \(\varepsilon^{3/4}\) on the full bounded \(C^2\) two-node torus class when every intervention log-ratio has Morse critical points?
seed_details.proof_boundary: The exact CauCA proof differentiates an equality and divides by an almost-everywhere nonzero discrepancy. The first changed step replaces division near isolated zeros by a weighted coercivity inequality that uses the synthetic determinant equation to control the divergence-free remainder.

seed_details.rebuttal: Their proof is qualitative and divides exact score identities by the discrepancy; it gives no stability when the derivative approaches zero, while their counterexample uses a positive-measure plateau rather than isolated Morse zeros.

Replace the matrix-well defect by the determinant residual plus Morse-weighted coordinate transport residuals.
literature_map.writing_arc_used: Nonlinear mixing leaves arbitrary reparameterizations; interventions create coordinate signatures; plateaus preserve rotations; isolated critical holes call for a quantitative rather than qualitative boundary.

literature_map.exact_target_status: No inspected source derives \((k+1)/(k+m+1)\) or any finite-type exponent for causal representation recovery.

For higher-order profiles, use the explicit finite-type margin and attained-order condition, then adapt critical-hole interpolation and localized volume-preserving twists without treating the finite-type hierarchy as a corollary of quantitative Morse theory.
